funFacts.imageAlt: Close-up view of fresh ripe Wisconsin cranberries during harvest season

facts.title: Native to Wisconsin
facts.description: Cranberries are native to Wisconsin's marshlands and have been harvested by Native Americans for centuries for food, medicine, and fabric dye.

facts.title: #1 in America
facts.description: Wisconsin has been the nation's leading cranberry producer for over 31 consecutive years, producing around 2/3 of the U.S. crop annually.

facts.title: Rich in Vitamin C
facts.description: One cup of raw cranberries provides 25% of your daily requirement of vitamin C. Sailors once ate cranberries to prevent scurvy at sea.

facts.title: Antioxidant Powerhouse
facts.description: Cranberries are well known for being rich in antioxidants and other beneficial compounds that support health and wellness.

facts.title: Family-Farmed
facts.description: Wisconsin's 250+ cranberry operations are primarily family farms, some of which have been in operation for over 100 years.

facts.title: "Crane Berry"
facts.description: European settlers named the fruit "crane berry" because the plant's stem and blossom resembled a sandhill crane.

consumerCta.title: Looking for Consumer Resources?
consumerCta.description: For recipes, festival information, cranberry products, and more consumer-focused content, visit the Wisconsin State Cranberry Growers Association at wiscran.org.
